title: HADOOP-18340. deleteOnExit does not work with S3AFileSystem
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect `deleteOnExit` to work uniformly across Hadoop filesystems, but on S3A the registered paths were not actually being removed when the filesystem closed.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A should honor `deleteOnExit` registrations the same way other Hadoop filesystems do, including for tracked paths that need to be deleted during shutdown. The filesystem should manage its own pending `deleteOnExit` set and use the same deletion semantics as normal deletes, without forcing callers to remember a separate cleanup path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A path registered through `deleteOnExit` should be deleted when the S3A filesystem is closed, and the implementation should route that cleanup through the same deletion logic used for ordinary removals via `deleteWithoutCloseCheck`. If the path was never present, close should remain safe rather than turning the shutdown into a new failure.

  '

title: HADOOP-18168. Fix S3A ITestMarkerTool dep. on purged public bucket, introduce PublicDatasetTestUtils
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The S3A public-dataset tests currently depend on a bucket layout that has been cleaned up, which makes previously stable requester-pays and marker-tool coverage unreliable. Test maintainers need those suites to point at a still-valid public dataset and to have one place that defines which public bucket and object should be used for each scenario.


  ## Desired outcome

  The S3A test utilities should provide a shared `PublicDatasetTestUtils` helper that supplies the configured public-dataset locations for cases such as requester-pays access and large public buckets with many objects. The default requester-pays path should move to a working public dataset, while still allowing environments to override those locations or skip the tests where requester-pays or AWS-specific assumptions do not apply.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The requester-pays coverage uses a valid public object again, marker-tool tests can obtain their public dataset locations through `PublicDatasetTestUtils`, configurable overrides remain available for different environments, and incompatible environments can skip these dataset-dependent tests instead of failing against a purged bucket.

  '

title: HADOOP-18397. Shutdown AWSSecurityTokenService when its resources are no longer in use
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  S3A components that request temporary credentials create AWS STS clients, but those clients may remain open longer than necessary and leak resources in long-running processes.


  ## Desired outcome

  The STS path should close `AWSSecurityTokenService` resources when they are no longer needed so repeated temporary-credential operations do not accumulate unused clients. This should be a resource-lifecycle improvement only; the credentials returned to callers and the retry behavior around STS requests must remain the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Code paths that create an STS client connection should close it deterministically after use, including the request-session-credentials flow. Temporary credential requests should continue to succeed and fail in the same user-visible ways, just without leaking STS resources afterward.

  '

title: HADOOP-17945. JsonSerialization raises EOFException reading JSON data stored on google GCS
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators sometimes read JSON state from object stores such as GCS and encounter zero-byte objects, where a raw end-of-file failure does not say which path was empty.


  ## Desired outcome

  When `JsonSerialization.load(...)` is asked to read an empty JSON file, it should fail with a path-aware `PathIOException` that clearly says `No data in ...` instead of surfacing a bare `EOFException`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Both load paths report the file that had no content, and callers no longer have to infer from a low-level EOF that the JSON object was empty.

  '

### common-log-placeholders
title: HADOOP-18387. Fix incorrect placeholder in hadoop-common
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Several common-module log statements use placeholder formatting incorrectly, which can suppress stack traces or produce noisy, low-value output during operational failures.


  ## Desired outcome

  These logging calls should be corrected so exceptions are passed as throwables rather than interpolated into malformed placeholders. This is observability cleanup only; it should not change the control flow or user-visible behavior of the affected filesystem and service-client paths.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The corrected log statements should preserve their existing messages while attaching the exception object properly, such as `Exception in removeRenewAction.` and `Error initialize YARN Service Client.` with stack traces available to operators.

  '
### bad-block-exception-logging
title: HDFS-16501. Print the exception when reporting a bad block
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When a DataNode''s volume scanner detects a bad block and reports it upstream, operators can currently see that the report happened but not why the block was considered bad. That leaves too little information in the logs to diagnose disk, checksum, or read-path problems during triage.


  ## Desired outcome

  The warning emitted while reporting a bad block should include the underlying exception so the reason for the failure is preserved in the log entry. This is an observability improvement only: the block should still be reported the same way, but the log must carry the original cause.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A bad-block report still occurs, the warning log now includes the exception details that triggered it, and operators can diagnose the failure from the DataNode log without reproducing the scan manually.

  '
### balancer-standby-namenode-logging
title: HDFS-16584.Record StandbyNameNode information when Balancer is running.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running the Balancer in HA deployments need to know which standby NameNode the tool is talking to when it gathers block and datanode information.

  ## Desired outcome

  Balancer logging should include the standby node’s `remoteAddress` when those HA RPCs succeed, so troubleshooting can distinguish active and standby interactions.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Balancer output for standby-side requests records the standby remote address instead of hiding it behind the active endpoint.

  '
### bpserviceactor-register-namenode-log
title: HDFS-16627. Improve BPServiceActor#register log to add NameNode address.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Registration logs from a DataNode do not always say which NameNode address they refer to, which makes startup and reconnect troubleshooting harder in HA and multi-NameNode environments.


  ## Desired outcome

  Handshake, connection-problem, and successful-registration log messages should all include the target NameNode address so operators can trace each registration attempt to a specific endpoint.


  ## Acceptance signals

  An operator reading the logs can tell from a single registration-related message which NameNode the DataNode was contacting.

  '
### datanode-log-placeholder
title: HDFS-16712. Fix incorrect placeholder in DataNode.java
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When disk balancer status cannot be read, the DataNode log message currently uses an incorrect placeholder pattern that hides the exception details operators need.


  ## Desired outcome

  That debug log should record the failure correctly so the exception is attached as a throwable instead of being formatted into a broken placeholder. This is a logging fix only; it must not change the DataNode response returned to callers.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A failed disk balancer status read should emit `Reading diskbalancer Status failed.` with the exception attached to the log event, and the user-facing behavior of returning an empty status string should remain unchanged.

  '
### httpprobe-resolved-host-logs
title: YARN-9971.YARN Native Service HttpProbe logs THIS_HOST in error messages
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  YARN Native Service health-check failures can still log the placeholder `THIS_HOST`, which hides the real endpoint that the probe actually tried to reach.


  ## Desired outcome

  `HttpProbe` failures should log the fully resolved host string after token substitution so operators can see the exact URL or host that failed for that container instance.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When an HTTP probe errors, the failure message names the concrete resolved host rather than the unresolved `THIS_HOST` placeholder.

  '
### retry-count-logging
title: HADOOP-18191. Log retry count while handling exceptions in RetryInvocationHandler
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When Hadoop clients hit retried RPC failures, operators and developers rely on retry logs to understand whether a call is briefly flapping or exhausting repeated attempts. The current log messages include exception and failover details, but they do not say which retry attempt produced the message, which makes incident analysis and retry tuning harder.


  ## Desired outcome

  Retry logging should include the current retry count whenever `RetryInvocationHandler` reports an exception-handling event. This is an observability improvement only, so retry behavior, failover decisions, and backoff timing must remain unchanged while the logs become more informative.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Retry-related log messages now include the retry count alongside the existing failure context, operators can distinguish early retries from repeated retries from the logs alone, and the underlying retry and failover behavior is otherwise unchanged.

  '
### setreplication-debug-string
title: HDFS-16530. setReplication debug log creates a new string even if debug is disabled
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operations that adjust replication can pass through very hot code paths, so even debug-only logging should avoid unnecessary work when debug logging is disabled. Today the set-replication path can still build path strings just to prepare a debug message that will never be emitted.


  ## Desired outcome

  The replication-change debug logging should incur no path-string construction cost unless debug logging is actually enabled. This is a small performance cleanup only, so the visible debug messages and replication behavior must stay the same whenever debug logging is turned on.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Disabled debug logging no longer forces path-string creation in the set-replication path, enabled debug logging still emits the same replication messages as before, and the replication operation itself is otherwise unchanged.

  '
### rpc-reader-call-debuglog
title: HADOOP-18082.Add debug log when RPC#Reader gets a Call.
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HADOOP-18082.Add debug log when RPC#Reader gets a Call.


  ### Description of PR

  Log some information from the moment Call enters the RPC inside, which will help us understand more about Call.

  The records here should be in the form of logs. The priority of the logs should not be too high, and debugging is the best.

  Details: HADOOP-18082


  ### How was this patch tested?

  Corresponding to the test, the pressure is not large.

  '

Apache Hadoop Compatibility
===========================

<!-- MACRO{toc|fromDepth=0|toDepth=3} -->

Purpose
-------

This document captures the compatibility goals of the Apache Hadoop project.
The different types of compatibility between Hadoop releases that affect
Hadoop developers, downstream projects, and end-users are enumerated. For each
type of compatibility this document will:

* describe the impact on downstream projects or end-users
* where applicable, call out the policy adopted by the Hadoop developers when incompatible changes are permitted.

All Hadoop interfaces are classified according to the intended audience and
stability in order to maintain compatibility with previous releases. See the
[Hadoop Interface Taxonomy](./InterfaceClassification.html) for details
about the classifications.

### Target Audience

This document is intended for consumption by the Hadoop developer community.
This document describes the lens through which changes to the Hadoop project
should be viewed. In order for end users and third party developers to have
confidence about cross-release compatibility, the developer community must
ensure that development efforts adhere to these policies. It is the
responsibility of the project committers to validate that all changes either
maintain compatibility or are explicitly marked as incompatible.

Within a component Hadoop developers are free to use Private and Limited Private
APIs, but when using components from a different module Hadoop developers
should follow the same guidelines as third-party developers: do not
use Private or Limited Private (unless explicitly allowed) interfaces and
prefer instead Stable interfaces to Evolving or Unstable interfaces where
possible. Where not possible, the preferred solution is to expand the audience
of the API rather than introducing or perpetuating an exception to these
compatibility guidelines. When working within a Maven module Hadoop developers
should observe where possible the same level of restraint with regard to
using components located in other Maven modules.

Above all, Hadoop developers must be mindful of the impact of their changes.
Stable interfaces must not change between major releases. Evolving interfaces
must not change between minor releases. New classes and components must be
labeled appropriately for audience and stability. See the
[Hadoop Interface Taxonomy](./InterfaceClassification.html) for details about
when the various labels are appropriate. As a general rule, all new interfaces
and APIs should have the most limited labels (e.g. Private Unstable) that will
not inhibit the intent of the interface or API.

### Structure

This document is arranged in sections according to the various compatibility
concerns. Within each section an introductory text explains what compatibility
means in that section, why it's important, and what the intent to support
compatibility is. The subsequent "Policy" section then sets forth in specific
terms what the governing policy is.

### Notational Conventions

The key words "MUST" "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD",
"SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as
described in [RFC 2119](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

Apache Hadoop Compatibility
===========================

<!-- MACRO{toc|fromDepth=0|toDepth=3} -->

Purpose
-------

This purpose of this document is to distill down the
[Hadoop Compatibility Guidelines](./Compatibility.html) into the information
relevant for a system administrator.

### Target Audience

The target audience is administrators who are responsible for maintaining
Apache Hadoop clusters and who must plan for and execute cluster upgrades.

Hadoop Releases
---------------

The Hadoop development community periodically produces new Hadoop releases to
introduce new functionality and fix existing issues. Realeses fall into three
categories:

* Major: a major release will typically include significant new functionality and generally represents the largest upgrade compatibility risk. A major release increments the first number of the release version, e.g. going from 2.8.2 to 3.0.0.
* Minor: a minor release will typically include some new functionality as well as fixes for some notable issues. A minor release should not pose much upgrade risk in most cases. A minor release increments the middle number of release version, e.g. going from 2.8.2 to 2.9.0.
* Maintenance: a maintenance release should not include any new functionality. The purpose of a maintenance release is to resolve a set of issues that are deemed by the developer community to be significant enough to be worth pushing a new release to address them. Maintenance releases should pose very little upgrade risk. A maintenance release increments the final number in the release version, e.g. going from 2.8.2 to 2.8.3.

Platform Dependencies
---------------------

The set of native components on which Hadoop depends is considered part of the
Hadoop ABI. The Hadoop development community endeavors to maintain ABI
compatibility to the fullest extent possible. Between minor releases the
minimum supported version numbers for Hadoop's native dependencies will not
be increased unless necessary, such as for security or licensing issues. When
such changes occur, the Hadoop developer community to try to keep the same
major version and only update the minor version.

Hadoop depends on the Java virtual machine. The minimum supported
version of the JVM will not change between major releases of Hadoop. In the
event that the current minimum supported JVM version becomes unsupported
between major releases, the minimum supported JVM version may be changed in a
minor release.

Network
-------

Hadoop has dependencies on some transport level technologies, such as SSL. The
minimum supported version of these dependencies will not
be increased unless necessary, such as for security or licensing issues. When
such changes occur, the Hadoop developer community to try to keep the same
major version and only update the minor version.

Service port numbers for Hadoop will remain the same within a major version,
though may be changed in a major release.

Hadoop's internal wire protocols will be maintained as backward and forward
compatible across minor releases within the same major version, both between
clients and servers and between servers, with the intent of enabling rolling
upgrades. Forward and backward compatibility of wire protocols across major
releases may be possible and may allow for rolling upgrades under certain
conditions, but no guarantees are made.

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  This is compatibility maintenance for Hadoop’s Netty integration, where request-handling behavior must stay stable while deprecated APIs are retired.

  ## Desired outcome

  Internal HTTP request processing should use the modern `uri()` accessor everywhere instead of deprecated `getUri()`, without changing authorization, query parsing, or response semantics.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing handlers continue to accept and reject requests exactly as before.

  '

title: HADOOP-18024. SocketChannel is not closed when IOException happens in Server$Listener.doAccept
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  If the IPC listener accepts a connection and then hits an IOException while configuring the SocketChannel, the server can leak that accepted socket. Over time, those leaked channels can waste file descriptors and destabilize busy servers.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure an accepted SocketChannel is closed whenever listener-side socket configuration fails, while keeping the listener loop alive and logging the failure. This is a robustness fix and should not change successful connection handling.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A forced IOException during listener accept configuration leaves no dangling accepted channel behind, and the server continues running after logging the problem.

  '

=== close-socketchannel-on-ioexception.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18024. SocketChannel is not closed when IOException happens in Server$Listener.doAccept
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  If the IPC listener accepts a connection and then hits an IOException while configuring the SocketChannel, the server can leak that accepted socket. Over time, those leaked channels can waste file descriptors and destabilize busy servers.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure an accepted SocketChannel is closed whenever listener-side socket configuration fails, while keeping the listener loop alive and logging the failure. This is a robustness fix and should not change successful connection handling.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A forced IOException during listener accept configuration leaves no dangling accepted channel behind, and the server continues running after logging the problem.

  '
=== bpserviceactor-register-namenode-log.yaml ===
title: HDFS-16627. Improve BPServiceActor#register log to add NameNode address.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Registration logs from a DataNode do not always say which NameNode address they refer to, which makes startup and reconnect troubleshooting harder in HA and multi-NameNode environments.


  ## Desired outcome

  Handshake, connection-problem, and successful-registration log messages should all include the target NameNode address so operators can trace each registration attempt to a specific endpoint.


  ## Acceptance signals

  An operator reading the logs can tell from a single registration-related message which NameNode the DataNode was contacting.

  '
=== httprequest-uri-accessor.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18249. Fix getUri() in HttpRequest has been deprecated.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  This is compatibility maintenance for Hadoop’s Netty integration, where request-handling behavior must stay stable while deprecated APIs are retired.

  ## Desired outcome

  Internal HTTP request processing should use the modern `uri()` accessor everywhere instead of deprecated `getUri()`, without changing authorization, query parsing, or response semantics.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing handlers continue to accept and reject requests exactly as before.

  '
=== compatibility-guide-link.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-16515. Update the link to compatibility guide
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Developers and operators reading Hadoop’s generated protocol documentation use the compatibility-guide link to understand what client/server upgrade combinations are supported.

  ## Desired outcome

  Those references should send readers to the current compatibility guide instead of an outdated or broken destination, so upgrade guidance is immediately usable wherever these protocol docs are surfaced.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The generated documentation consistently points to the compatibility guide and no stale compatibility URL remains in these protocol definitions.

  '

A Deprecated interface could potentially be removed in the future and should
not be used.  Even so, a Deprecated interface will continue to function until
it is removed.  When a Deprecated interface can be removed depends on whether
it is also Stable, Evolving, or Unstable.

How are the Classifications Recorded?
-------------------------------------

How will the classification be recorded for Hadoop APIs?

* Each interface or class will have the audience and stability recorded using
  annotations in the org.apache.hadoop.classification package.

* The javadoc generated by the maven target javadoc:javadoc lists only the
  public API.

* One can derive the audience of java classes and java interfaces by the
  audience of the package in which they are contained. Hence it is useful to
  declare the audience of each java package as public or private (along with the
  private audience variations).

How will the classification be recorded for other interfaces, such as CLIs?

* See the [Hadoop Compatibility](Compatibility.html) page for details.

FAQ
---

* Why aren’t the java scopes (private, package private and public) good enough?
    * Java’s scoping is not very complete. One is often forced to make a class
      public in order for other internal components to use it. It also does not
      have friends or sub-package-private like C++.

* But I can easily access a Private interface if it is Java public. Where is the
  protection and control?

item.aggregated_output:
Overview
--------

  DistCp (distributed copy) is a tool used for large
  inter/intra-cluster copying. It uses MapReduce to effect its distribution,
  error handling and recovery, and reporting. It expands a list of files and
  directories into input to map tasks, each of which will copy a partition of
  the files specified in the source list.

  [The erstwhile implementation of DistCp]
  (http://hadoop.apache.org/docs/r1.2.1/distcp.html) has its share of quirks
  and drawbacks, both in its usage, as well as its extensibility and
  performance. The purpose of the DistCp refactor was to fix these
  shortcomings, enabling it to be used and extended programmatically. New
  paradigms have been introduced to improve runtime and setup performance,
  while simultaneously retaining the legacy behaviour as default.

  This document aims to describe the design of the new DistCp, its spanking new
  features, their optimal use, and any deviance from the legacy implementation.


---

    hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/1 32
    hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/2 32
    hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/10 64
    hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/20 32

  And destination/sizes:

    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/1 32
    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/10 32
    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/20 64

  Will effect:

    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/1 32
    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/2 32
    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/10 64
    hdfs://nn2:8020/target/20 32

  `1` is skipped because the file-length and contents match. `2` is copied
  because it doesn't exist at the target. `10` and `20` are overwritten since
  the contents don't match the source.

  If `-update` is used, `1` is skipped because the file-length and contents match. `2` is copied because it doesn’t exist at the target. `10` and `20` are overwritten since the contents don’t match the source. However, if `-append` is additionally used, then only `10` is overwritten (source length less than destination) and `20` is appended with the change in file (if the files match up to the destination's original length).

  If `-overwrite` is used, `1` is overwritten as well.

$H3 Sync

  `-diff` option syncs files from a source cluster to a target cluster with a
  snapshot diff. It copies, renames and removes files in the snapshot diff list.

  `-update` option must be included when `-diff` option is in use.

  Most cloud providers don't work well with sync at the moment.


---
    hadoop distcp -update -diff snap1 snap2 /src/ /dst/

  The command above should succeed. `1.txt` will be copied from `/src/` to
  `/dst/`. Again, `-update` option is required.

  If we run the same command again, we will get `DistCp sync failed` exception
  because the destination has added a new file `1.txt` since `snap1`. That
  being said, if we remove `1.txt` manually from `/dst/` and run the sync, the
  command will succeed.

$H4 Experiment 2: syncing diff of two non-adjacent snapshots

  First do a clean up from Experiment 1.

    hdfs dfs -rm -skipTrash /dst/1.txt

  Run sync command, note the `<to_snapshot>` has been changed from `snap2` in
  Experiment 1 to `snap3`.

    hadoop distcp -update -diff snap1 snap3 /src/ /dst/


---

     * A file with the same name doesn't exist at target.
     * A file with the same name exists at target, but has a different file
       size.
     * A file with the same name exists at target, but has a different
       checksum, and `-skipcrccheck` isn't mentioned.
     * A file with the same name exists at target, but `-overwrite` is
       specified.
     * A file with the same name exists at target, but differs in block-size
       (and block-size needs to be preserved.

  * **CopyCommitter:** This class is responsible for the commit-phase of the
    DistCp job, including:

     * Preservation of directory-permissions (if specified in the options)

---
  As has been mentioned in the preceding, should a map fail to copy one of its
  inputs, there will be several side-effects.

  * Unless `-overwrite` is specified, files successfully copied by a previous
    map on a re-execution will be marked as "skipped".
  * If a map fails `mapreduce.map.maxattempts` times, the remaining map tasks

title: 'HADOOP-18202. create-release fails fatal: unsafe repository'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Release managers running Hadoop''s containerized release flow can now hit Git''s post-CVE ownership protection, where commands fail with `fatal: unsafe repository` because the mounted source tree inside the container is owned by a different user. That blocks the release workflow even though the checkout location is expected and controlled.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `create-release` workflow should trust the mounted source checkout at `/build/source` so containerized release builds can proceed without manual Git intervention. This is release-tooling compatibility work only, so the release process and output should stay the same apart from eliminating the unsafe-repository failure.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running the release script in the supported containerized setup no longer fails with `fatal: unsafe repository`, Git treats `/build/source` as an allowed checkout for the workflow, and the rest of the release process behaves exactly as before.

  '

=== gson-2-9-0.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18300. Upgrade Gson dependency to version 2.9.0
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Build metadata and packaged notices should describe the same Gson version so maintainers, release tooling, and downstream consumers are not left reconciling mixed dependency information.


  ## Desired outcome

  The project should consistently use Gson 2.9.0 wherever the shared dependency version and related binary-license metadata are declared.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Both the build configuration and the shipped dependency metadata identify Gson 2.9.0 as the version in use.

  '
=== dependency-check-7-1-1.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18297. Upgrade dependency-check-maven to 7.1.1
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Build owners want dependency scanning to stay current without introducing unnecessary churn into the rest of the Hadoop build.


  ## Desired outcome

  Upgrade the root build to use `dependency-check-maven` version `7.1.1` so security scans run on the newer tooling while normal Hadoop behavior stays the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Maven-based dependency scans now run with `dependency-check-maven` `7.1.1`, and the change behaves as tooling maintenance rather than a functional product change.

  '
=== maven-site-plugin-3-11-0.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-17551. Upgrade maven-site-plugin to 3.11.0
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop''s site-generation build depends on the Maven Site Plugin, and keeping that plugin current helps maintainers avoid older build-tool behavior without changing the generated project itself. This is build maintenance in the documentation pipeline, not a product feature change.


  ## Desired outcome

  The build should use `maven-site-plugin` version `3.11.0` in place of the older declaration, while preserving the existing site-generation workflow and published content expectations.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Build metadata references `maven-site-plugin` `3.11.0`, site generation continues to run through the normal Maven flow, and there are no user-visible Hadoop behavior changes beyond the plugin upgrade.

  '
=== jquery-ui-1-13-1.yaml ===
title: YARN-11092. Upgrade jquery ui to 1.13.1
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  YARN web UI pages rely on jQuery UI widgets, and operators expect the bundled administration interface to stay current with supported browser behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  The packaged jQuery UI asset should move to version 1.13.1 while preserving the existing `JQueryUI` rendering flow and widget behavior used by Hadoop pages.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The UI loads `jquery-ui-1.13.1.custom.min.js`, and the existing widgets continue to behave the same way.

  '
=== moment-js-2-29-2.yaml ===
title: HDFS-16562. Upgrade moment.min.js to 2.29.2
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The HDFS web UI bundles Moment.js for browser-side date handling, and operators expect the shipped admin interface to use a maintained library version.

  ## Desired outcome

  The packaged `moment.min.js` asset should move to 2.29.2 without changing the surrounding Hadoop UI flow or requiring any page-level rewiring.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The web application serves the 2.29.2 bundle and existing timestamp rendering behavior continues to work.

  '
=== aws-sdk-1-12-262.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18344. Upgrade AWS SDK to 1.12.262
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop’s S3A integration depends on the AWS Java SDK, and periodic SDK upgrades are needed to stay aligned with upstream fixes and service behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  This dependency update should move the AWS SDK baseline to `1.12.262` without changing the user-facing S3A contract. Existing filesystem semantics, configuration keys, and application behavior should remain stable while the dependency stack is refreshed.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Builds and test runs should consume AWS SDK `1.12.262`, and S3A functionality should continue to behave the same from the caller’s perspective after the upgrade.

  '

title: HDFS-16384. Upgrade Netty to 4.1.72.Final
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop components that rely on Netty need the upgraded 4.1.x line to avoid compatibility issues, but the module layout has to stay coherent for downstream consumers.

  ## Desired outcome

  The Netty stack should move to `4.1.72.Final` with the matching module set instead of leaving callers with a partially upgraded transport layer.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The aligned dependency set includes the expected supporting pieces such as `netty-codec-socks` and `netty-handler-proxy`, all at `4.1.72.Final`.

  '

title: HDFS-16384. Upgrade Netty to 4.1.72.Final
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop components that rely on Netty need the upgraded 4.1.x line to avoid compatibility issues, but the module layout has to stay coherent for downstream consumers.

  ## Desired outcome

  The Netty stack should move to `4.1.72.Final` with the matching module set instead of leaving callers with a partially upgraded transport layer.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The aligned dependency set includes the expected supporting pieces such as `netty-codec-socks` and `netty-handler-proxy`, all at `4.1.72.Final`.

  '

  This is dependency maintenance for build and diff tooling, not a runtime feature change.

title: HADOOP-18240. Upgrade Yetus to 0.14.0
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop committers and CI operators depend on Yetus for patch validation, precommit analysis, and release checks.

  ## Desired outcome

  The project’s Yetus baseline should move to 0.14.0 so review and CI tooling runs against the maintained analyzer version without changing Hadoop runtime behavior.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Precommit and related automation use Yetus 0.14.0 successfully.

  '

=== hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction.yaml ===
title: HDFS-16256. Minor fix in HDFSFederationBalance document
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using HDFS federation balancing docs depend on the written guidance being accurate, especially when they are following procedural documentation during cluster maintenance. A small documentation error in the FedBalance material can still create confusion in an operational workflow.


  ## Desired outcome

  The HDFS Federation Balance documentation should be corrected so the affected guidance reads accurately and consistently. This is a documentation-only fix, so the balancing feature itself and its operational behavior must remain unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The incorrect text in the HDFSFederationBalance documentation is corrected, the surrounding guidance reads cleanly for operators following the document, and no runtime behavior or command semantics change.

  '

=== numa-enable-documentation.yaml ===
title: YARN-11195. Adding document to enable numa
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators enabling NUMA-aware scheduling in YARN need clear guidance about prerequisites, topology sources, and the configuration choices involved before they can turn the feature on safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  The documentation should explain when NUMA awareness is appropriate, what executor prerequisites apply, how to enable it, and how the NodeManager can discover or accept NUMA topology information.


  ## Acceptance signals

  An operator can use the shipped guidance to enable NUMA awareness deliberately, choose the intended topology source, and understand the required configuration points without hunting through implementation details.

  '

=== powershellfencer-documentation.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-18314. Add some description for PowerShellFencer.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Administrators configuring HA fencing on Windows need the built-in fencing choices to be documented as clearly as the Unix-oriented methods so they can choose a supported option without guesswork.


  ## Desired outcome

  The HA and default-configuration documentation should describe `powershell(...)` as a supported fencing method on Windows and explain what kind of process identifier it expects.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A Windows operator can discover `powershell(...)` directly in the shipped fencing documentation and understand how to configure it confidently for NameNode fencing.

  '

=== slow-datanode-metrics-docs.yaml ===
title: HDFS-16526. Addendum Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators can only make use of new DataNode slow-path counters if the metrics reference material describes them clearly enough to wire dashboards and alerts against the published names. After adding the slow DataNode metrics, the user-facing metrics documentation also needs to acknowledge those counters.


  ## Desired outcome

  Hadoop''s metrics reference should document the new slow DataNode counters so operators know that `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` are available and what conditions they represent. This is documentation-only work, so runtime behavior and metric emission stay unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The metrics documentation includes the newly added slow DataNode counters by name, operators can discover `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` from the published reference material, and no code behavior changes beyond that documentation update.

  '

=== config-prefix-examples.yaml ===
title: HADOOP-17479. Fix the examples of hadoop config prefix

  The build metadata marks Jackson 1 as a runtime dependency, artifacts still resolve and run as before, and no functional behavior changes are introduced beyond narrowing the dependency scope.

YARN (YET ANOTHER RESOURCE NEGOTIATOR or YARN Application Resource Negotiator)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Requirements
-------------
Java: JDK 1.6
Maven: Maven 3

Setup
-----
Install protobuf 2.5.0 (Download from http://code.google.com/p/protobuf/downloads/list)
 - install the protoc executable (configure, make, make install)
 - install the maven artifact (cd java; mvn install)


Quick Maven Tips
----------------
clean workspace: mvn clean
compile and test: mvn install
skip tests: mvn install -DskipTests
skip test execution but compile: mvn install -Dmaven.test.skip.exec=true
clean and test: mvn clean install
run selected test after compile: mvn test -Dtest=TestClassName (combined: mvn clean install -Dtest=TestClassName)
create runnable binaries after install: mvn assembly:assembly -Pnative (combined: mvn clean install assembly:assembly -Pnative)

Eclipse Projects
----------------
http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-ide-eclipse.html

1. Generate .project and .classpath files in all maven modules
mvn eclipse:eclipse
CAUTION: If the project structure has changed from your previous workspace, clean up all .project and .classpath files recursively. Then run:
mvn eclipse:eclipse

2. Import the projects in eclipse.

3. Set the environment variable M2_REPO to point to your .m2/repository location.

NetBeans Projects
-----------------

NetBeans has builtin support of maven projects. Just "Open Project..."
and everything is setup automatically. Verified with NetBeans 6.9.1.


Custom Hadoop Dependencies
--------------------------

By default Hadoop dependencies are specified in the top-level pom.xml
properties section. One can override them via -Dhadoop-common.version=...
on the command line. ~/.m2/settings.xml can also be used to specify
these properties in different profiles, which is useful for IDEs.

Modules
-------
YARN consists of multiple modules. The modules are listed below as per the directory structure:

hadoop-yarn-api - YARN's cross platform external interface

hadoop-yarn-common - Utilities which can be used by yarn clients and server

hadoop-yarn-server - Implementation of the hadoop-yarn-api
	hadoop-yarn-server-common - APIs shared between resourcemanager and nodemanager
	hadoop-yarn-server-nodemanager (TaskTracker replacement)
	hadoop-yarn-server-resourcemanager (JobTracker replacement)

Utilities for understanding the code
------------------------------------
Almost all of the yarn components as well as the mapreduce framework use
state-machines for all the data objects. To understand those central pieces of
the code, a visual representation of the state-machines helps much. You can first
convert the state-machines into graphviz(.gv) format by
running:
   mvn compile -Pvisualize
Then you can use the dot program for generating directed graphs and convert the above
.gv files to images. The graphviz package has the needed dot program and related
utilites.For e.g., to generate png files you can run:
   dot -Tpng NodeManager.gv > NodeManager.png

./requirements/slow-datanode-metrics-docs.yaml:15:  The metrics documentation includes the newly added slow DataNode counters by name, operators can discover `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` from the published reference material, and no code behavior changes beyond that documentation update.
./requirements/slow-datanode-metrics.yaml:1:title: HDFS-16526. Add metrics for slow DataNode
./requirements/slow-datanode-metrics.yaml:5:  HDFS operators need clearer visibility into slow DataNode behavior so they can tell whether replication or write pipelines are being delayed by local disk work or by slow acknowledgements moving upstream through the pipeline. Without dedicated counters, these cases are harder to spot and diagnose from routine monitoring.
./requirements/slow-datanode-metrics.yaml:10:  DataNode metrics should expose separate counters for these slow-path conditions so monitoring systems can distinguish them directly. The exported metric contract needs to include `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` for delayed flush or sync activity and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` for delayed upstream acknowledgements, without changing normal write behavior.
./requirements/slow-datanode-metrics.yaml:15:  DataNode metrics now publish `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount`, slow flush-or-sync events increment the former, slow upstream-ack events increment the latter, and the change adds observability only without altering the underlying pipeline semantics.
./requirements/slownode-badnode-pipeline-recovery.yaml:5:  When a write pipeline keeps receiving acknowledgements from a slow DataNode, the client can remain stuck retrying the same unhealthy path instead of rebuilding around that node. Users want the pipeline to recover automatically before the write times out.
./requirements/slow-datanode-reconfigurable.yaml:5:  Avoiding slow DataNodes for reads is useful, but NameNode operators need to be able to turn that policy on or off without a restart.

-
-1. Generate .project and .classpath files in all maven modules
-mvn eclipse:eclipse
-CAUTION: If the project structure has changed from your previous workspace, clean up all .project and .classpath files recursively. Then run:
-mvn eclipse:eclipse
-
-2. Import the projects in eclipse.
-
-3. Set the environment variable M2_REPO to point to your .m2/repository location.
-
-NetBeans Projects
------------------
-
-NetBeans has builtin support of maven projects. Just "Open Project..."
-and everything is setup automatically. Verified with NetBeans 6.9.1.
-
-
-Custom Hadoop Dependencies
---------------------------
-
-By default Hadoop dependencies are specified in the top-level pom.xml
-properties section. One can override them via -Dhadoop-common.version=...
-on the command line. ~/.m2/settings.xml can also be used to specify
-these properties in different profiles, which is useful for IDEs.
-
-Modules
--------
-YARN consists of multiple modules. The modules are listed below as per the directory structure:
-
-hadoop-yarn-api - YARN's cross platform external interface
-
-hadoop-yarn-common - Utilities which can be used by yarn clients and server
-
-hadoop-yarn-server - Implementation of the hadoop-yarn-api
-	hadoop-yarn-server-common - APIs shared between resourcemanager and nodemanager
-	hadoop-yarn-server-nodemanager (TaskTracker replacement)
-	hadoop-yarn-server-resourcemanager (JobTracker replacement)
-
-Utilities for understanding the code
-------------------------------------
-Almost all of the yarn components as well as the mapreduce framework use
-state-machines for all the data objects. To understand those central pieces of
-the code, a visual representation of the state-machines helps much. You can first
-convert the state-machines into graphviz(.gv) format by
-running:
-   mvn compile -Pvisualize
-Then you can use the dot program for generating directed graphs and convert the above
-.gv files to images. The graphviz package has the needed dot program and related
-utilites.For e.g., to generate png files you can run:
-   dot -Tpng NodeManager.gv > NodeManager.png

item.text: I’m doing one broader apply-scan across the still-open requirements so I don’t miss any remaining clean cherry-picks. That should tell me where to spend the manual effort next.

item.command:
/bin/bash -c 'cd /workspace && rem=$(comm -23 <(find requirements -maxdepth 1 -name '"'*.yaml' -printf '%f\\n' | sed 's/\\.yaml"'$//'"' | sort) <(find requirement_patches -maxdepth 1 -name '*.diff' -size +0c -printf '%f\\n' | sed 's/\\.diff"'$//'"' | sort))
: > /tmp/remaining-apply.tsv
while read -r slug; do
  [ -z \""'$slug" ] && continue
  id=$(sed -n "s/''^title: '"\\([A-Z][A-Z0-9-]*-[0-9][0-9]*\\).*/\\1/p\" \"requirements/"'${slug}.yaml" | head -1)
  sha=
  if [ -n "$id" ]; then
    sha=$(git log --format='"'%H' upstream/trunk --grep=\""'$id" -n 1)
    if [ -z "$sha" ]; then sha=$(git log --format='"'%H' upstream/branch-3.4 --grep=\""'$id" -n 1); fi
    if [ -z "$sha" ]; then sha=$(git log --format='"'%H' upstream/branch-3.3 --grep=\""'$id" -n 1); fi
  fi
  status=NOJIRA
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    if curl -s -L "https://github.com/apache/hadoop/commit/${sha}.patch" | git apply --check - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      status=PASS
    else
      status=FAIL
    fi
  fi
  printf '"'%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' \""'$slug" "$id" "$sha" "$status" >> /tmp/remaining-apply.tsv
  if [ "$status" = PASS ]; then printf '"'PASS %s %s\\n' \""'$slug" "$sha"; fi
done <<< "$rem"
wc -l /tmp/remaining-apply.tsv && grep $'"'\\tPASS"'$'"' /tmp/remaining-apply.tsv | sed 's/\\t/ /g'"
